change.summary: Zoom stopped returning email VALUES for participants flagged as guests across roughly 30 REST endpoints and 9 webhook events. The fields email, participant_email and user_email still exist and still return 200 — they return an empty string instead of an address. Confirmed from a developer's own response body: GET /v2/report/meetings/{meetingId}/participants now yields "user_email": "".

spec.note: This is the case that breaks schema monitoring. Zoom published a Swagger 2.0 spec and it could not possibly have shown this change: same status codes, same field names, same JSON shape, same types. Only the values went empty. A spec diff is structurally blind to it. Scored as a miss for the spec signal, which is exactly right.

changelog.note: 34 days of notice — but it never reached the developer forum's Announcements category, verified by enumerating every topic created there from 2021-11 to 2022-03 (all 22 are SDK release notes). Developers subscribed to the channel Zoom told them to subscribe to got nothing.

contract.note: Detectable only by asserting on VALUES, not shape or status. A probe would have to record that user_email was a non-empty string and is now empty. Account-gated: it needs a real meeting with a real external participant, so the fixture has to be constructed, not merely fetched.

notes: announced_at is Zoom's self-reported publication date on a page that has since been migrated; the original announcements page was client-rendered so its archive snapshots carry no article text to check it against. effective_at is independently corroborated — the first developer report was filed 2022-03-01T09:30:15Z, the same day, and Zoom staff first replied 16 days later. Zoom repeated the pattern on 2023-03-03 by hiding participant IDs, which broke the correlate-by-ID workaround people adopted after this one. The entire announcement trail is now dead on the live web and survives only in Wayback.
